comprehensiveness.criterion: Coverage of the current clinical trial landscape across major programs, sponsors, phases, and cancer indications
Coverage of mechanisms of action relevant to mRNA cancer vaccines
Coverage of delivery systems and formulation approaches used clinically
Coverage of early efficacy signals from clinical studies
Coverage of safety and immunogenicity evidence as part of the clinical evidence base
Coverage of major therapeutic design paradigms and clinical use settings
Coverage of the translational and development context shaping the field

insight.criterion: Analytical linkage between mechanism, antigen strategy, delivery system, and clinical outcomes
Quality of interpretation of early efficacy signals
Critical evaluation of strengths, limitations, and translational bottlenecks
Soundness and logical consistency of conclusions
Usefulness and originality of higher-level judgments or future-oriented takeaways

instruction_following.criterion: Direct response to the stated research question
Coverage of all four explicitly requested topical components
Adherence to requested report structure and markdown conventions
Presence of a dedicated Sources section listing consulted references/URLs
Scope discipline and relevance to current mRNA cancer vaccines

readability.criterion: Logical organization and navigability: The report is structured with clear sections and subsections, smooth transitions, and an argument sequence that helps readers move from clinical trial landscape to mechanisms of action, target antigens, delivery systems, and early efficacy signals without confusion.

Clarity and precision of prose: The article uses precise, straightforward wording, defines clinical and immunological terms (e.g., neoantigen, adjuvant, immunogenicity) when first introduced, and avoids unnecessary medical jargon or unexplained acronyms.

Digestibility of complex information: Complex oncological and molecular concepts, such as mRNA vaccine mechanisms and antigen selection strategies, are presented clearly with appropriate examples, comparisons, and visual aids that support comprehension.

Effective use of markdown formatting and visual hierarchy: Markdown headings, bullet points, tables, emphasis, and topic sentences are used appropriately to highlight trial data, comparative results, and critical evaluations across different vaccine platforms.

Terminology management and explanation of technical concepts: Medical and technical terms are used consistently, defined when first introduced, and explained at a level appropriate for an informed reader interested in mRNA cancer vaccine development.

Cohesion, transitions, and signposting: Sentences are concise and varied in length, paragraphs are focused on one main idea, and dense clinical material is broken into digestible units with clear transitions that reduce reader fatigue.

Audience-appropriate exposition: The level of detail and terminology are tailored to an informed research audience, with sufficient background provided for readers to understand mRNA cancer vaccine mechanisms and clinical trial data without requiring specialized oncology expertise.
